learning_objective: 🎯 Learn that 'honour among thieves' is a myth! Watch how a clever burglar gets outsmarted by an even cleverer thief.

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: परागकणों से होने वाली एलर्जी (छींक आना)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Horace is a 50-year-old unmarried, respectable lock-maker. But he has a secret: he robs one safe every year to buy rare and expensive books.
Horace plans to rob a house called Shotover Grange. He knows everything about the house, the dog, and the safe. However, he suffers from 'hay fever', which makes him sneeze near flowers.
While robbing, a young, confident lady in a red dress appears. She acts like the owner's wife and catches him. She promises to let him go if he opens the safe for her, claiming she forgot the code.
Fearing prison, Horace opens the safe without his gloves to please her. The lady takes the jewels. Two days later, Horace is arrested because his fingerprints are all over the room!
The lady in red was NOT the owner's wife; she was just another thief! She cleverly used Horace to do the hard work and take the blame.

fun_activity.title: 🎭 Spot the Liar
fun_activity.instructions: The lady in red was acting very confidently, patting the dog and arranging ornaments. Write down 2 clues Horace *should* have noticed to realize she wasn't the real owner!

exam_tips: 📌 Understand Horace's character: He was 'good and respectable—but not completely honest'.
📌 Why didn't Horace wear gloves? (He panicked and took them off to light the lady's cigarette, breaking his own rule).
📌 Discuss the irony of the phrase 'honour among thieves' in the context of this story.
quick_recap: ⭐ Horace only stole from those who had a lot of money and never hurt anyone.
⭐ The real wife of the house owner was a sharp-tongued, grey-haired woman of 60.
⭐ Horace now works as an assistant librarian in the prison, hating the phrase 'honour among thieves'.
